_readme: 英文版：按 id（指标按 key）对照 eras.json、milestones.json、metrics.json 里给读者看的文字；没写的字段沿用中文。forecastBy 对应 forecast.by，sourceName 对应 source.name。改中文时同步改这里。

big-bang.title: The Big Bang
big-bang.summary: The universe expands from an extremely hot, dense state, and the first atoms form as it cools. There are no stars yet, and no observers.

first-stars-galaxies.title: First Stars and Galaxies
first-stars-galaxies.summary: The first stars ignite and forge heavy elements; galaxies gradually assemble, and the Milky Way begins to take shape.

solar-system.title: Formation of the Solar System
solar-system.summary: The Sun and planets are born from a molecular cloud; Earth and the Moon form in turn, their primordial surfaces scorching and barren.

origin-of-life.title: Origin of Life on Earth
origin-of-life.summary: Single-celled life persists for about 3 billion years; photosynthesis brings oxygen to the atmosphere, and eukaryotic cells appear.

cambrian-explosion.title: The Cambrian Explosion
cambrian-explosion.summary: Complex animals proliferate, plants and animals move onto land in turn, and life begins to reshape the entire planet.

dinosaurs-mammals.title: Dinosaurs and Mammals
dinosaurs-mammals.summary: Dinosaurs rule the land for more than 100 million years; after an asteroid impact, mammals rise and primates appear.
dinosaurs-mammals.artStyle: Late Triassic ecosystem reconstruction oil painting

homo-stone-tools.title: Homo and Stone Tools
homo-stone-tools.summary: Hominins walk upright and knap stone tools, and Homo erectus leaves Africa. Tools begin to extend the body, but there is still no reliable energy source.

taming-fire.title: Taming Fire
taming-fire.summary: Fire lets people cook, keep warm, ward off animals and light the night: the first energy source humans mastered outside their own bodies.

sapiens-language.title: Homo sapiens and Language
sapiens-language.summary: Homo sapiens emerges in Africa; language and social cooperation gradually develop, though people still live as small bands of hunter-gatherers.

cognitive-revolution.title: Cognitive Revolution and Cave Art
cognitive-revolution.summary: Modern humans leave Africa and spread across every continent, leaving murals and symbolic objects; imagination and stories begin to pass down the generations.

agricultural-revolution.title: The Agricultural Revolution
agricultural-revolution.summary: With domesticated crops and livestock, people settle in villages and populations grow; food surpluses make specialization and cities possible.

cities-writing.title: Cities and Writing
cities-writing.summary: Cities, the wheel, bronze and writing appear in Mesopotamia, so accounts, laws and history can be recorded.

iron-age.title: Iron, Alphabets and Coinage
iron-age.summary: Ironworking spreads and iron tools and weapons become common; alphabets and coinage appear in turn, and large states expand.
iron-age.artStyle: Near Eastern early ironworking clay relief

axial-age.title: The Axial Age
axial-age.summary: Philosophy and science flourish in Greece, China, India and elsewhere, and geometry and law take shape, but power still comes from human, animal and water power.

medieval-silk-road.title: The Middle Ages and the Silk Road
medieval-silk-road.summary: The Silk Road links Europe and Asia, and technologies such as paper, gunpowder, the compass and movable type spread between civilizations.

printing.title: The Printing Press
printing.summary: The printing press makes books cheap to mass-produce and knowledge spreads far faster; the Age of Discovery binds the continents together.

scientific-revolution.title: The Scientific Revolution
scientific-revolution.summary: Heliocentrism, the telescope and Newtonian mechanics establish the method of experiment plus mathematics, and nature becomes predictable.

steam-age.title: The Age of Steam
steam-age.summary: Coal and the steam engine bring the first large-scale use of fossil energy, and factories and railways transform production and distance.

electric-age.title: The Electrical Age
electric-age.summary: Generators, power grids, electric light and the telephone spread, and energy and information can travel instantly along wires.

combustion-flight.title: Internal Combustion and Flight
combustion-flight.summary: Cars, airplanes and synthetic ammonia transform travel and the food supply, and oil becomes the main energy source.

atomic-age.title: The Atomic Age
atomic-age.summary: Nuclear fission releases atomic energy; nuclear weapons and nuclear power arrive together, and humanity for the first time holds power enough to destroy civilization.

transistor-computer.title: The Transistor and the Computer
transistor-computer.summary: Electronic computers and the transistor appear, information theory and artificial intelligence are proposed, and computation begins to be automated.

space-age.title: The Space Age
space-age.summary: Satellites, human spaceflight and the Moon landing take humanity off the ground; integrated circuits and computer networks grow behind the scenes.

personal-computer.title: The Personal Computer
personal-computer.summary: The microprocessor brings computers into homes and offices, and ordinary people can program, write and process data.

internet.title: The Internet
internet.summary: The World Wide Web and search engines connect the world's information, and the cost of accessing knowledge plummets.

social-web.title: Social Networks
social-web.summary: Blogs, social networks, video sites and online shopping let ordinary people publish content and run shops, and the internet shifts from browsing to participation.

mobile-internet.title: The Mobile Internet
mobile-internet.summary: Smartphones and cloud computing keep billions of people online at all times, and data volumes grow explosively.

deep-learning.title: Deep Learning
deep-learning.summary: GPU-trained neural networks achieve breakthroughs in image and speech recognition, and residual networks then make much deeper models trainable.

deep-reinforcement-learning.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning and AlphaGo
deep-reinforcement-learning.summary: Deep networks are combined with reinforcement learning, and AlphaGo defeats Lee Sedol at Go, bringing machines' ability to learn strategy into public view.

transformer.title: The Transformer
transformer.summary: The attention architecture lets models process sequences more efficiently and becomes the technical foundation of later large language models; it is not yet a chat assistant for the general public.

pretraining.title: Language Pretraining
pretraining.summary: GPT and BERT first learn from large amounts of unlabeled text and are then adapted to specific tasks, turning language models from specialized tools into reusable foundations.

foundation-models.title: Scaling and Few-Shot Learning
foundation-models.summary: GPT-3 handles many language tasks from a prompt and a few examples, and AlphaFold 2 shows deep learning's breakthrough potential in scientific research.

ai-copilots.title: AI Coding Assistants
ai-copilots.summary: Copilot brings code generation into the editor, moving AI from lab demos into everyday workflows as programmers get suggestions from natural language and context.

generative-ai.title: Generative Images
generative-ai.summary: DALL·E 2, Midjourney and Stable Diffusion turn text into images, giving painting and design generative tools the general public can use.

large-models.title: Conversational Large Models
large-models.summary: Instruction tuning and human feedback make language models better at following user intent, and ChatGPT brings writing, Q&A and programming into ordinary people's daily lives.

multimodal.title: Multimodal Large Models
multimodal.summary: GPT-4 demonstrates image understanding as language models begin to connect text and vision, and models such as Gemini push multimodal capabilities further.

tool-use.title: Tool Use
tool-use.summary: Function calling arrives in large-model APIs, letting models call external programs to look up information, run code and take actions, paving the way for agentic workflows.

generative-video.title: Generative Video
generative-video.summary: Sora shows progress in text-to-video generation as generated content moves from still frames to continuous shots; demo capabilities still fall short of practical usability.

realtime-multimodal.title: Real-Time Voice and Vision
realtime-multimodal.summary: GPT-4o demonstrates low-latency voice and vision interaction, and AI assistants begin moving from typing and waiting for answers toward more natural real-time conversation.

reasoning.title: Reasoning Models
reasoning.summary: o1 makes reasoning compute before answering a new scaling direction, improving math and coding ability; reasoning performance still needs case-by-case verification.

agents.title: AI Agents
agents.summary: AI begins operating computers autonomously, programming for hours on end and solving hard math problems, while frontier models iterate week by week.

agent-teams-speculative.title: Long-Horizon Agent Teams (speculative)
agent-teams-speculative.summary: Scenario forecast (2027–2029): teams of agents may continuously divide up, check and deliver work in software development and research. This assumes mature permissions, verification and failure recovery; humans remain responsible for complex tasks.

personal-ai-speculative.title: Personal AI and On-Device Coordination (speculative)
personal-ai-speculative.summary: Scenario forecast (2027–2030): personal assistants may coordinate across phones and computers, with more everyday tasks done on-device. Adoption depends on power consumption, privacy permissions and reliable memory; complex tasks may still rely on the cloud.

controlled-robotics-speculative.title: Robots in Controlled Settings (speculative)
controlled-robotics-speculative.summary: Scenario forecast (2028–2031): robots in warehouses, factories and labs may take on more multi-step operations, expanding first in roles with controlled environments. Cost, safety and fault handling still limit adoption; a robot in every home is not the baseline scenario.

science-loop-speculative.title: Closed-Loop AI Research (speculative)
science-loop-speculative.summary: Scenario forecast (2029–2031): in some materials and life-science projects, AI may link hypotheses, experimental design and result analysis, with automated equipment shortening iterations. Only reproducible experimental validation counts as a breakthrough, and it does not mean drugs will be approved right away.

grid-compute-speculative.title: Coordinated Build-Out of Compute and Grid (speculative)
grid-compute-speculative.summary: Scenario forecast (2028–2031): AI demand may drive a coordinated build-out of data centers, power grids, energy storage and cooling. The IEA's 2030 electricity demand projections ground the demand side; the build-out pace in this e-acc.ai scenario remains constrained by grid connection, financing and supply chains, and does not imply energy has become limitlessly cheap.

interactive-worlds-speculative.title: Interactive Worlds and Simulation Training (speculative)
interactive-worlds-speculative.summary: Scenario forecast (2029–2031): interactive generated worlds may be used for creative work, training and robot simulation. Long-term consistency, physical accuracy and cost will determine where they are usable; a playable scene is not a trustworthy simulation of reality.

abundance-speculative.title: Energy and Compute Abundance (speculative)
abundance-speculative.summary: Speculative: if fusion, solar and AI keep advancing, energy and compute could become extremely cheap; nothing is settled yet.

kardashev-i-speculative.title: Toward Kardashev Type I (speculative)
kardashev-i-speculative.summary: Speculative: a Type I civilization needs about 10¹⁶ watts, roughly 500 times today's level; at historical growth rates that is still centuries away, so this only marks the direction.

big-bang.title: The Big Bang
big-bang.detail: The universe began expanding from an extremely hot, dense state about 13.787 billion years ago.

cosmic-microwave-background.title: The Universe Becomes Transparent
cosmic-microwave-background.detail: About 380,000 years after the Big Bang, atoms formed and light began to travel freely, leaving behind the cosmic microwave background.

first-stars.title: The First Stars Ignite
first-stars.detail: About 100 million years after the Big Bang, the first stars formed and forged heavier elements.

milky-way-forms.title: The Milky Way Begins to Form
milky-way-forms.detail: The seeds of the Milky Way appeared about 13.6 billion years ago, giving birth to its oldest stars.

solar-system-forms.title: The Solar System Forms
solar-system-forms.detail: About 4.568 billion years ago, a molecular cloud collapsed into the Sun and the disk of planets around it.

earth-forms.title: Earth Forms
earth-forms.detail: Earth accreted from material in the protoplanetary disk and is about 4.54 billion years old.

moon-forms.title: The Moon Forms
moon-forms.detail: The leading hypothesis holds that a Mars-sized body struck the early Earth, and the debris coalesced into the Moon.

earliest-life.title: Earliest Evidence of Life
earliest-life.detail: Stromatolites and other fossils show that life on Earth had appeared at least 3.5 billion years ago.

great-oxidation-event.title: The Great Oxidation Event
great-oxidation-event.detail: Photosynthesis by cyanobacteria let free oxygen accumulate in the atmosphere for the first time.

eukaryotes.title: Eukaryotic Cells Appear
eukaryotes.detail: Complex cells with a nucleus emerged; the earliest likely fossils date to about 1.8 to 1.6 billion years ago.

ediacaran-biota.title: The Ediacaran Biota
ediacaran-biota.detail: About 575 million years ago, early large multicellular organisms diversified on the seafloor.

cambrian-explosion.title: The Cambrian Explosion
cambrian-explosion.detail: Most modern animal phyla appeared within a geologically brief span of time.

land-plants.title: Plants Colonize Land
land-plants.detail: Spore fossils of land plants appear in the Middle Ordovician, and the land begins to turn green.

tiktaalik.title: Fish Move onto Land
tiktaalik.detail: Tiktaalik combined features of fish and tetrapods, showing vertebrates evolving toward life on land.

permian-extinction.title: The End-Permian Extinction
permian-extinction.detail: The most severe mass extinction in Earth's history wiped out most marine species.

first-dinosaurs.title: Dinosaurs Appear
first-dinosaurs.detail: Dinosaurs arose in the Late Triassic and went on to dominate the land for more than 100 million years.

first-mammals.title: Mammals Appear
first-mammals.detail: Mammals evolved from cynodonts, with origins tracing back to the Late Triassic.

k-pg-extinction.title: The End-Cretaceous Extinction
k-pg-extinction.detail: After an asteroid impact, the non-avian dinosaurs died out and mammals went on to flourish.

early-primates.title: Early Primates
early-primates.detail: One of the earliest known primate fossils comes from Africa, about 57 million years ago.

sahelanthropus.title: Humans and Chimpanzees Diverge
sahelanthropus.detail: Sahelanthropus tchadensis lived about 7 million years ago, near the start of the human lineage.

lomekwi-tools.title: The Earliest Stone Tools
lomekwi-tools.detail: Knapped stone tools about 3.3 million years old were unearthed at Lomekwi, Kenya.

lucy.title: Lucy
lucy.detail: The Australopithecus afarensis fossil known as "Lucy" shows that early hominins already walked upright.

oldowan.title: Oldowan Tools
oldowan.detail: The earliest systematic stone-tool tradition, beginning about 2.9 million years ago.

homo-erectus.title: Homo erectus
homo-erectus.detail: Homo erectus had body proportions close to modern humans and is generally regarded as the first hominin to leave Africa.

acheulean.title: Acheulean Hand Axes
acheulean.detail: Symmetrical bifacial hand axes appeared about 1.76 million years ago, as toolmaking turned to deliberate design.

control-of-fire.title: Control of Fire
control-of-fire.detail: Evidence from Wonderwerk Cave in South Africa shows that the genus Homo was using fire at least about 1 million years ago.

homo-sapiens.title: Homo sapiens Emerges
homo-sapiens.detail: Early Homo sapiens fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, date to about 315,000 years ago.

out-of-africa.title: Out of Africa
out-of-africa.detail: About 70,000 to 50,000 years ago, modern humans spread from Africa across the world.

oldest-figurative-art.title: The Oldest Narrative Painting
oldest-figurative-art.detail: A cave scene of humans and a wild pig in Sulawesi is at least 51,200 years old.

chauvet-cave.title: Chauvet Cave Paintings
chauvet-cave.detail: France's Chauvet Cave holds a wealth of animal paintings, most dating to about 37,000 to 33,500 years ago.

agriculture.title: The Origins of Agriculture
agriculture.detail: Crops were domesticated in the Fertile Crescent around 10,000 to 8000 BC, and people gradually settled down.

gobekli-tepe.title: Göbekli Tepe
gobekli-tepe.detail: A megalithic complex in present-day Turkey, built around 9500 BC.

catalhoyuk.title: Çatalhöyük
catalhoyuk.detail: From about 7100 BC, a large Neolithic settlement grew up in Anatolia.

wheel.title: The Wheel
wheel.detail: By around 3500 BC, wheels were recorded in use in Sumer.

bronze-age.title: The Bronze Age
bronze-age.detail: Around 3300 BC, the Near East entered the Bronze Age, bringing harder tools and weapons.

cuneiform.title: Cuneiform
cuneiform.detail: Around 3200 BC, the Sumerians began keeping records on clay tablets, developing the earliest known writing.

great-pyramid.title: The Great Pyramid of Giza
great-pyramid.detail: Completed around 2560 BC, it remained the tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years.

code-of-hammurabi.title: The Code of Hammurabi
code-of-hammurabi.detail: A written Babylonian law code carved on a stone stele, around 1753 BC.

iron-age.title: The Iron Age
iron-age.detail: From around 1200 BC, ironworking spread and iron gradually replaced bronze.
iron-age.artStyle: Near Eastern early ironworking clay relief

phoenician-alphabet.title: The Phoenician Alphabet
phoenician-alphabet.detail: A handful of letters could record speech sounds; it later gave rise to the Greek, Latin and other alphabets.

coinage.title: Coinage
coinage.detail: Around 600 BC, electrum coins appeared in Lydia, while China was already casting bronze spade money.

euclid-elements.title: Euclid's Elements
euclid-elements.detail: Euclid derived theorems from axioms, setting the model for deductive reasoning.

watermill.title: The Waterwheel
watermill.detail: Water-driven wheels appear in the writings of the Greek engineer Philo, around the 3rd century BC.

antikythera-mechanism.title: The Antikythera Mechanism
antikythera-mechanism.detail: A geared device from the 2nd century BC that predicted celestial events; it is the oldest known analog computer.

papermaking.title: Cai Lun Improves Papermaking
papermaking.detail: In the Eastern Han, Cai Lun improved papermaking using tree bark, hemp scraps and rags, making writing material cheap.

zero.title: Rules for Computing with Zero
zero.detail: The Indian mathematician Brahmagupta set out rules for arithmetic involving zero.

windmill.title: The Windmill
windmill.detail: Around the 9th century, horizontal windmills appeared in Persia, used to grind grain and lift water.

diamond-sutra.title: The Woodblock-Printed Diamond Sutra
diamond-sutra.detail: Dated 11 May 868, this Diamond Sutra is the earliest surviving complete printed book with an explicit date. It demonstrates mature woodblock reproduction of words and images, rather than the invention of printing.

gunpowder-warfare.title: Gunpowder in Warfare
gunpowder-warfare.detail: Invented by Chinese Taoist alchemists, gunpowder was first used in warfare around 904.
gunpowder-warfare.artStyle: Song dynasty fine-brush painting on silk

movable-type.title: Movable Type
movable-type.detail: Around 1040, Bi Sheng of the Northern Song invented movable type made of baked clay.
movable-type.artStyle: Song dynasty fine-brush painting on silk

magnetic-compass.title: The Magnetic Compass
magnetic-compass.detail: Shen Kuo gave the first written description of the magnetic needle compass in his Dream Pool Essays.
magnetic-compass.artStyle: Song dynasty fine-brush painting on silk

gutenberg-press.title: The Gutenberg Press
gutenberg-press.detail: Around 1440, Gutenberg invented the printing press, and books began to be reproduced at scale.

columbus.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
columbus.detail: A transatlantic route opened, beginning sustained contact between the Old World and the New.

circumnavigation.title: The First Circumnavigation
circumnavigation.detail: The remnants of Magellan's fleet, led by Elcano, returned to Spain, completing the first voyage around the world.

copernicus.title: Heliocentrism
copernicus.detail: Copernicus published On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres, placing the Sun rather than Earth at the center.

sidereus-nuncius.title: Galileo Turns a Telescope to the Sky
sidereus-nuncius.detail: Sidereus Nuncius was published, recording mountains on the Moon and the moons of Jupiter.

newton-principia.title: Principia Mathematica
newton-principia.detail: Newton set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation, describing heaven and Earth with the same mathematics.

coke-smelting.title: Coke Smelting of Iron
coke-smelting.detail: Abraham Darby smelted iron in a coke-fired blast furnace, and coal began to replace charcoal.

newcomen-engine.title: The Newcomen Steam Engine
newcomen-engine.detail: The first practical steam engine, used to pump water from mines.

encyclopedie.title: The Encyclopédie
encyclopedie.detail: Diderot and his collaborators began publishing the Encyclopédie, a systematic compendium of the knowledge of the age.

watt-engine.title: Watt's Separate Condenser
watt-engine.detail: Watt received a patent that greatly improved steam-engine efficiency; the engine later came to power factories.

smallpox-vaccination.title: Cowpox Inoculation
smallpox-vaccination.detail: Jenner inoculated an 8-year-old boy with cowpox to protect him against smallpox, giving rise to vaccines.

voltaic-pile.title: The Voltaic Pile
voltaic-pile.detail: The first battery able to supply a continuous electric current.

jacquard-loom.title: The Jacquard Mechanism Becomes Practical
jacquard-loom.detail: After demonstrating his mechanism in 1801, Jacquard brought punched-card-controlled weaving into practical use around 1804. Changing the card chain changed the pattern, providing a precedent for programmable machines.

first-locomotive.title: The First Locomotive-Hauled Train
first-locomotive.detail: Trevithick's steam locomotive pulled a train along a tramway in Wales.

difference-engine.title: The Difference Engine
difference-engine.detail: Babbage proposed a machine to compute mathematical tables automatically.

liverpool-manchester-railway.title: The First Intercity Railway
liverpool-manchester-railway.detail: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened, running entirely on steam locomotives to a timetable.

electromagnetic-induction.title: Electromagnetic Induction
electromagnetic-induction.detail: Faraday discovered that a changing magnetic field produces an electric current, the principle behind the generator.

daguerreotype.title: Photography Unveiled
daguerreotype.detail: The French Academy of Sciences announced Daguerre's daguerreotype process.

ada-lovelace-program.title: The First Computer Program
ada-lovelace-program.detail: Lovelace wrote an algorithm for the Analytical Engine to compute Bernoulli numbers.

morse-telegraph.title: The Telegraph Line Opens
morse-telegraph.detail: Morse sent a message from Washington to Baltimore: "What hath God wrought!"

boolean-logic.title: Boolean Algebra
boolean-logic.detail: Boole published The Laws of Thought, showing that logical reasoning can be carried out with algebra.

drake-well.title: The Drake Well
drake-well.detail: A well drilled in Pennsylvania struck oil, launching the modern petroleum industry.

origin-of-species.title: On the Origin of Species
origin-of-species.detail: Darwin proposed natural selection to explain the evolution of species.

maxwell-equations.title: Electromagnetic Field Theory
maxwell-equations.detail: Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism and light, and predicted electromagnetic waves.

transatlantic-cable.title: Transatlantic Telegraph
transatlantic-cable.detail: A permanent undersea cable entered service, under the slogan "From two weeks to two minutes."

periodic-table.title: The Periodic Table
periodic-table.detail: Mendeleev presented his periodic table to the Russian Chemical Society and predicted undiscovered elements.

telephone.title: The Telephone
telephone.detail: Bell transmitted speech by telephone for the first time.

light-bulb.title: The Practical Light Bulb
light-bulb.detail: Edison's team developed a long-lasting carbon-filament incandescent lamp.

koch-tuberculosis.title: The Tuberculosis Bacillus Discovered
koch-tuberculosis.detail: Koch announced that tuberculosis is caused by a bacterium, establishing the germ theory of disease.

pearl-street-station.title: The First Commercial Power Station
pearl-street-station.detail: Edison's Pearl Street Station began supplying electricity to customers in Manhattan.

benz-motorwagen.title: The Automobile
benz-motorwagen.detail: Karl Benz patented a three-wheeled car powered by an internal combustion engine.

hollerith-tabulator.title: The Punched-Card Tabulator
hollerith-tabulator.detail: The US Census processed its data with Hollerith's tabulating machines.

x-rays.title: X-Rays
x-rays.detail: Röntgen discovered X-rays, letting doctors see inside the human body for the first time.

marconi-transatlantic.title: Transatlantic Radio
marconi-transatlantic.detail: Marconi received in Newfoundland a radio signal sent from England.

wright-flyer.title: Powered Flight
wright-flyer.detail: The Wright brothers achieved the first powered, controlled, crewed flight.

special-relativity.title: Special Relativity
special-relativity.detail: Einstein proposed special relativity and mass–energy equivalence.

haber-bosch.title: Industrial Ammonia Synthesis
haber-bosch.detail: The Haber process went into production at BASF's Oppau plant, making large-scale nitrogen fertilizer possible.

assembly-line.title: The Moving Assembly Line
assembly-line.detail: Ford adopted the moving assembly line, turning the car into a mass-market product.

kdka-broadcast.title: Commercial Broadcasting
kdka-broadcast.detail: Pittsburgh's KDKA broadcast the results of the US presidential election.

television.title: Television
television.detail: Baird demonstrated the world's first mechanical television system in London.

penicillin.title: Penicillin
penicillin.detail: Fleming discovered penicillin, ushering in the age of antibiotics.

hubble-law.title: The Expanding Universe
hubble-law.detail: Hubble publishes observations showing that galaxies recede at speeds proportional to their distance.

turing-machine.title: The Turing Machine
turing-machine.detail: Turing proposes a mathematical model of computability, laying the foundation of computer science.
turing-machine.artStyle: 1930s academic photographic style with an ink diagram

nuclear-fission.title: Nuclear Fission Discovered
nuclear-fission.detail: Hahn and Strassmann discover that uranium nuclei can split.

chicago-pile-1.title: First Nuclear Reactor
chicago-pile-1.detail: Chicago Pile-1 achieves the first man-made self-sustaining chain reaction.

trinity-test.title: First Nuclear Test
trinity-test.detail: The Trinity test detonates the first atomic bomb in New Mexico.

eniac.title: ENIAC Unveiled
eniac.detail: ENIAC, a general-purpose electronic computer, is publicly unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania.

transistor.title: The Transistor
transistor.detail: Bardeen and Brattain at Bell Labs build the point-contact transistor.

information-theory.title: Information Theory
information-theory.detail: Shannon publishes "A Mathematical Theory of Communication": information becomes measurable.

manchester-baby.title: The First Electronic Stored Program Runs
manchester-baby.detail: The University of Manchester's experimental Baby computer successfully ran a program held in electronic memory, demonstrating a computing approach in which both instructions and data reside in the machine.

turing-test.title: The Turing Test
turing-test.detail: Turing publishes "Computing Machinery and Intelligence", proposing the "imitation game".

dna-double-helix.title: The DNA Double Helix
dna-double-helix.detail: Watson and Crick publish the molecular structure of DNA in Nature.

silicon-solar-cell.title: Practical Solar Cell
silicon-solar-cell.detail: Bell Labs publicly demonstrates the first practical photovoltaic cell.

obninsk.title: Nuclear Power Plant Online
obninsk.detail: The Soviet Obninsk plant goes online, the first to feed nuclear power into an electricity grid.

dartmouth-workshop.title: "Artificial Intelligence" Is Born
dartmouth-workshop.detail: The Dartmouth Summer Research Project convenes, and artificial intelligence becomes a field of research.

perceptron.title: The Perceptron
perceptron.detail: Rosenblatt proposes the perceptron, a machine that learns from data.

integrated-circuit.title: The Integrated Circuit
integrated-circuit.detail: Kilby demonstrates the first integrated circuit prototype.

mosfet.title: The MOS Field-Effect Transistor Is Built
mosfet.detail: Atalla and Kahng at Bell Labs built a working metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor in 1959 and publicly demonstrated it in 1960. MOS fabrication later became the basis of high-density chips.

laser.title: The Laser
laser.detail: Maiman builds the first laser at Hughes Research Laboratories.

gagarin.title: First Human in Space
gagarin.detail: Gagarin orbits the Earth once aboard Vostok 1.

moores-law.title: Moore's Law
moores-law.detail: Moore predicts that the number of components on a chip will double at a regular interval.

eliza.title: ELIZA
eliza.detail: Weizenbaum releases ELIZA, an early chatbot.

green-revolution.title: The "Green Revolution"
green-revolution.detail: High-yield crop varieties, fertilizers and irrigation spread; the term "Green Revolution" is coined this year.

apollo-11.title: Moon Landing
apollo-11.detail: Apollo 11 astronauts Armstrong and Aldrin walk on the lunar surface.

arpanet-first-message.title: First ARPANET Message
arpanet-first-message.detail: UCLA sends the first network message to the Stanford Research Institute.

intel-4004.title: The Microprocessor
intel-4004.detail: The Intel 4004 puts a central processing unit on a single chip.

first-mobile-call.title: First Mobile Phone Call
first-mobile-call.detail: Motorola's Martin Cooper makes the first public call on a handheld mobile phone.

apple-ii.title: Apple II Goes on Sale
apple-ii.detail: Ready-made personal computers for the general public begin to spread.

smallpox-eradicated.title: Smallpox Eradicated
smallpox-eradicated.detail: The World Health Organization certifies the global eradication of smallpox.

xcon.title: Expert Systems Enter Industry
xcon.detail: DEC begins using the XCON configuration system in its plants, bringing rule-based AI into commercial use.

ibm-pc.title: IBM PC
ibm-pc.detail: IBM launches its Personal Computer, and its compatibles become the de facto standard.

tcp-ip.title: TCP/IP Switch-On
tcp-ip.detail: ARPANET officially switches to TCP/IP, and the internet protocol suite takes shape.

backpropagation.title: Backpropagation
backpropagation.detail: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams publish a method for training multilayer networks in Nature.

hubble-launch.title: Hubble Space Telescope Launched
hubble-launch.detail: Orbiting above the atmosphere, the telescope delivers sharp images of deep space and measures the expansion rate of the universe.

lithium-ion-battery.title: Lithium-Ion Batteries Commercialized
lithium-ion-battery.detail: Sony introduces the commercial lithium-ion battery, giving phones, laptops and electric cars a lightweight power source.

world-wide-web.title: The World Wide Web Goes Public
world-wide-web.detail: Berners-Lee publicly releases the World Wide Web project.

linux.title: Linux Is Born
linux.detail: Torvalds announces his kernel project, which becomes the open-source foundation of servers and Android.

china-internet.title: China Connects to the Internet
china-internet.detail: China gains full-function access to the global internet via a 64K leased line.

dolly.title: Dolly the Sheep
dolly.detail: The first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell is born.

lstm.title: LSTM
lstm.detail: Long short-term memory networks let recurrent neural networks remember much longer sequences.

deep-blue.title: Deep Blue Beats Kasparov
deep-blue.detail: IBM's Deep Blue defeats the world chess champion in a regulation match.

prius.title: Prius Hybrid
prius.detail: Toyota launches the first mass-produced hybrid car in Japan, sharply cutting fuel consumption.

google.title: Google Founded
google.detail: The PageRank algorithm makes the vast web efficiently searchable.

oicq.title: OICQ Released
oicq.detail: Tencent releases its instant messenger (later renamed QQ), giving Chinese internet users an online chat tool.

wifi-80211b.title: Wi-Fi Standard Established
wifi-80211b.detail: IEEE 802.11b is approved, and wireless LANs begin to enter homes and offices.

gps-sa-off.title: Full GPS Accuracy for Civilians
gps-sa-off.detail: The US turns off Selective Availability, improving civilian positioning accuracy to about ten meters.

iss-crew.title: Permanent Crew in Space
iss-crew.detail: The first crew moves into the International Space Station; humans have been continuously present in low Earth orbit ever since.

wikipedia.title: Wikipedia Launches
wikipedia.detail: An encyclopedia that anyone can edit.

human-genome.title: Human Genome Project Completed
human-genome.detail: The sequence of the human genome is essentially complete.

taobao.title: Taobao Launches
taobao.detail: Individuals can open online shops and shop online, bringing e-commerce to ordinary Chinese households.

shenzhou-5.title: Shenzhou 5 Crewed Flight
shenzhou-5.detail: Yang Liwei goes to space, making China the third country to achieve independent human spaceflight.

alipay.title: Alipay Launches
alipay.detail: Escrow payments arrive on Taobao, solving the problem of trust in online shopping.

facebook.title: Facebook Launches
facebook.detail: A real-name social network lets people maintain their relationships online.

youtube.title: First YouTube Video
youtube.detail: Anyone can upload videos and watch them online.

amazon-s3.title: Cloud Computing
amazon-s3.detail: Amazon launches the S3 storage service; storage and compute can be rented on demand.

deep-autoencoder.title: Deep Learning Revival
deep-autoencoder.detail: Hinton and Salakhutdinov publish a method for training deep networks in Science.

ipsc.title: Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
ipsc.detail: Shinya Yamanaka uses four genes to reprogram adult cells into pluripotent stem cells.

iphone.title: iPhone Unveiled
iphone.detail: The touchscreen smartphone puts the internet in your pocket.

cuda.title: CUDA
cuda.detail: NVIDIA releases CUDA, opening GPUs to general-purpose computing.

kindle.title: Kindle Released
kindle.detail: An e-ink reader with wireless downloads holds hundreds or thousands of books at once.

app-store.title: App Store Opens
app-store.detail: Third-party apps install on phones with a single tap, and the mobile app ecosystem takes shape.

beijing-tianjin-hsr.title: Beijing–Tianjin Intercity Railway Opens
beijing-tianjin-hsr.detail: China's first 350 km/h high-speed line links Beijing and Tianjin in half an hour.

android.title: First Android Phone
android.detail: The HTC Dream, the first Android phone, is released; an open-source system brings smartphones to mass-market prices.

imagenet.title: ImageNet
imagenet.detail: Fei-Fei Li's team releases a large-scale labeled image dataset.

bitcoin.title: Bitcoin Genesis Block
bitcoin.detail: The first decentralized cryptocurrency network goes live.

china-3g.title: China Issues 3G Licenses
china-3g.detail: The three major carriers receive 3G licenses, and mobile internet use begins to spread.

wechat.title: WeChat Launches
wechat.detail: Free mobile instant messaging, later expanded into a platform for social networking, payments and mini programs.

watson-jeopardy.title: Watson Wins Jeopardy!
watson-jeopardy.detail: IBM's Watson defeats human champions on the TV quiz show.

crispr.title: CRISPR Gene Editing
crispr.detail: Doudna and Charpentier show that CRISPR-Cas9 can cut DNA at chosen sites.

tesla-model-s.title: Model S Deliveries
tesla-model-s.detail: An all-electric sedan with a range of about 400 km begins reaching customers.

higgs-boson.title: The Higgs Boson
higgs-boson.detail: CERN announces the discovery of the Higgs boson.

three-gorges.title: Three Gorges Dam Fully Operational
three-gorges.detail: The last main generating unit comes online, and the world's largest hydropower station reaches full output.

alexnet.title: AlexNet
alexnet.detail: A deep convolutional network trained on GPUs wins the ImageNet competition, slashing the error rate.

china-4g.title: China Issues 4G Licenses
china-4g.detail: The three major carriers receive TD-LTE licenses, and mobile video and live streaming become part of daily life.

wechat-hongbao.title: WeChat Red Envelopes
wechat-hongbao.detail: Grabbing red envelopes over Chinese New Year leads huge numbers of users to link bank cards and adopt mobile payments.

gan.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
gan.detail: Goodfellow and colleagues propose GANs, and machines begin generating realistic images.

gravitational-waves.title: Gravitational Waves Detected
gravitational-waves.detail: LIGO makes the first direct detection of gravitational waves, produced by a binary black hole merger.

resnet.title: ResNet: Residual Networks
resnet.detail: Residual connections make very deep neural networks easier to train; a 152-layer model achieves leading results on ImageNet.

falcon9-landing.title: First Rocket Booster Recovery
falcon9-landing.detail: A Falcon 9 first stage lands vertically after an orbital launch, making reusable rockets a reality.

alphago.title: AlphaGo Beats Lee Sedol
alphago.detail: AlphaGo defeats one of the world's top Go players 4–1.

mobike.title: Bike Sharing Launches
mobike.detail: Mobike launches in Shanghai: scan a code to unlock and return a bike, no docking station needed.

micius.title: Micius Quantum Satellite
micius.detail: The world's first quantum science satellite launches and achieves satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution.

douyin.title: Douyin Launches
douyin.detail: A short-video app lets ordinary people shoot, share and scroll through videos.

fast.title: FAST Telescope Completed
fast.detail: The Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope is completed, the world's largest single-dish radio telescope.

transformer.title: Transformer
transformer.detail: The paper "Attention Is All You Need" introduces the Transformer architecture.

falcon-heavy.title: Falcon Heavy Maiden Flight
falcon-heavy.detail: The most powerful operational rocket makes its first flight, and its two side boosters land in sync.

gpt-1.title: GPT-1
gpt-1.detail: OpenAI pretrains a language model on unlabeled text, then fine-tunes it for specific tasks.

bert.title: BERT
bert.detail: Google's bidirectional pretrained model sets new records on many language understanding tasks.

change-4.title: Chang'e 4 Lands on the Far Side of the Moon
change-4.detail: A spacecraft makes the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon.

gpt-2.title: GPT-2
gpt-2.detail: A 1.5-billion-parameter model writes coherent long-form text; OpenAI releases it in stages.

black-hole-image.title: First Image of a Black Hole
black-hole-image.detail: The Event Horizon Telescope releases an image of the shadow of the M87 black hole.

quantum-supremacy.title: Quantum Supremacy
quantum-supremacy.detail: Google's Sycamore processor outperforms classical supercomputers on a specific sampling task.

china-5g.title: 5G goes commercial in China
china-5g.detail: China's three major carriers launch 5G plans, beginning commercial 5G service.

rag.title: RAG: retrieval-augmented generation
rag.detail: Language models retrieve external documents before answering, so knowledge can come from an updatable library rather than only from what was memorized in training.

ddpm.title: A breakthrough for diffusion models
ddpm.detail: DDPM generates high-quality images by gradually removing noise, laying key groundwork for later diffusion-based image tools.

beidou-3.title: BeiDou-3 goes global
beidou-3.detail: The BeiDou satellite navigation system begins providing worldwide service.

alphafold-2.title: AlphaFold 2
alphafold-2.detail: Predicts protein structures with near-experimental accuracy at CASP14.

mrna-vaccine.title: mRNA vaccine approved
mrna-vaccine.detail: The UK authorizes the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, the first mRNA vaccine approved for use.

change-5.title: Chang'e 5 returns lunar soil
change-5.detail: China's first lunar sample-return mission brings back 1,731 grams of lunar soil.

zhurong.title: Zhurong lands on Mars
zhurong.detail: The Tianwen-1 lander soft-lands on Mars carrying the Zhurong rover.

github-copilot.title: Copilot preview
github-copilot.detail: AI completes code in the editor from context, giving programmers a coding assistant.

jwst-launch.title: James Webb Space Telescope launches
jwst-launch.detail: An infrared space telescope lifts off to observe the early universe.

instructgpt-paper.title: InstructGPT: training on human feedback
instructgpt-paper.detail: A paper describes training language models on human demonstrations and preference rankings so answers better follow user instructions; the approach was later used for ChatGPT.

eacc-born.title: e/acc is born
eacc-born.detail: Anonymous authors publish a case for effective accelerationism: build, accelerate, climb the Kardashev scale.

midjourney.title: Midjourney open beta
midjourney.detail: Striking images from a text prompt, now open to the public.

stable-diffusion.title: Stable Diffusion
stable-diffusion.detail: An image generation model released with open weights that runs on personal computers.

react.title: ReAct: reasoning and acting
react.detail: Models interleave reasoning with external actions and adjust their next step based on what comes back, becoming a key research path for tool-using agents.

tiangong-t.title: Tiangong space station takes shape
tiangong-t.detail: With the Mengtian module repositioned, China's space station completes its basic T-shaped configuration in orbit.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT launches
chatgpt.detail: OpenAI releases a conversational language model, bringing large language models to the public.

fusion-ignition.title: Fusion ignition
fusion-ignition.detail: The US National Ignition Facility produces more fusion energy than the laser energy delivered, for the first time.

llama.title: LLaMA
llama.detail: Meta releases LLaMA to researchers, sparking the open-weight model ecosystem.

gpt-4.title: GPT-4
gpt-4.detail: A multimodal model with a leap in capability, priced at launch at $30 per million input tokens.

claude-1.title: Claude released
claude-1.detail: Anthropic releases Claude, initially with limited access for partners.

starship-ift1.title: Starship's first integrated flight test
starship-ift1.detail: The largest rocket ever built launches as a full stack for the first time.

function-calling.title: Function calling comes to LLM APIs
function-calling.detail: OpenAI introduces structured function calling, letting developers connect models to lookups, calculations and other software tools.

techno-optimist-manifesto.title: The Techno-Optimist Manifesto
techno-optimist-manifesto.detail: Marc Andreessen publishes a manifesto calling for technology and markets to accelerate progress.

casgevy.title: First gene-editing therapy approved
casgevy.detail: The UK approves the CRISPR therapy Casgevy for sickle cell disease and thalassemia.

gemini.title: Gemini released
gemini.detail: Google launches Gemini, a natively multimodal large model.

neuralink-human.title: Neuralink's first human implant
neuralink-human.detail: Neuralink announces its first participant has received a wireless brain-computer interface implant, later showing cursor control by thought; other BCIs had already been studied in humans.

sora.title: Sora first shown
sora.detail: OpenAI previews a text-to-video model that generates minute-long HD video.

claude-3.title: Claude 3
claude-3.detail: Claude 3 Opus matches GPT-4; for the first time several labs share the frontier.

gpt-4o.title: GPT-4o
gpt-4o.detail: Natively handles voice, images and text, at half the API price of GPT-4 Turbo.

change-6.title: Chang'e 6 samples the far side
change-6.detail: Humanity's first samples returned from the far side of the Moon.

eu-ai-act.title: EU AI Act takes effect
eu-ai-act.detail: The first comprehensive AI law enters into force, with provisions applying in phases.

openai-o1.title: o1: reasoning models
openai-o1.detail: Models think before answering, making test-time compute a new scaling dimension.

nobel-physics-2024.title: Physics Nobel for neural networks
nobel-physics-2024.detail: Hopfield and Hinton are honored for foundational work on machine learning with artificial neural networks.

nobel-chemistry-2024.title: Chemistry Nobel for AlphaFold
nobel-chemistry-2024.detail: Hassabis and Jumper win for protein structure prediction, sharing the prize with Baker.

starship-catch.title: Launch tower catches a booster
starship-catch.detail: On Starship's fifth flight test, the Super Heavy booster returns to the launch tower and is caught by its mechanical arms.

computer-use.title: AI learns to use a computer
computer-use.detail: Anthropic introduces "computer use": the model can see the screen, move the cursor, click and type.

deepseek-v3.title: DeepSeek-V3
deepseek-v3.detail: An open-source large model reaching the frontier at low training cost.
deepseek-v3.artStyle: New Chinese ink wash with cool light

deepseek-r1.title: DeepSeek-R1 open-sourced
deepseek-r1.detail: A frontier-level reasoning model released with open weights under the MIT license.

stargate.title: Stargate: $500 billion
stargate.detail: SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle and MGX pledge $500 billion over four years to build AI data centers in the US.

claude-4.title: Claude 4
claude-4.detail: Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 launch, bringing long-running autonomous coding into production use.

imo-gold.title: AI reaches IMO gold level
imo-gold.detail: Gemini Deep Think solves 5 of 6 problems at the International Mathematical Olympiad, scoring 35 points.

gpt-5.title: GPT-5
gpt-5.detail: OpenAI unifies a reasoning model and a fast model behind a single router.

gpt-5-1.title: GPT-5.1
gpt-5-1.detail: An iteration of the GPT-5 series that adapts its reasoning effort to a problem's difficulty.

gemini-3.title: Gemini 3
gemini-3.detail: Google's frontier model takes another step, with stronger agentic coding and long-task abilities.

claude-opus-4-5.title: Claude Opus 4.5
claude-opus-4-5.detail: Released right after Gemini 3; the gap between frontier releases shrinks to weeks.

artemis-ii-record.title: Artemis II sets a record
artemis-ii-record.detail: Four astronauts fly around the Moon, breaking Apollo 13's record for the farthest humans have traveled.

gpt-5-5.title: GPT-5.5
gpt-5-5.detail: OpenAI's flagship update arrives in ChatGPT and Codex, with the API following the next day.

claude-fable-5.title: Claude Fable 5
claude-fable-5.detail: The Claude 5 series begins; the less restricted Mythos 5 is available only to safety and research partners.

gpt-5-6-preview.title: GPT-5.6 limited preview
gpt-5-6-preview.detail: Sol, Terra and Luna open first to about 20 partners vetted by the US government.

claude-sonnet-5.title: Claude Sonnet 5
claude-sonnet-5.detail: Near-Opus capability at a Sonnet price, aimed at running agents cheaply.

grok-4-5.title: Grok 4.5
grok-4-5.detail: xAI releases a 1.5-trillion-parameter model priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.

gpt-5-6-ga.title: GPT-5.6 general availability
gpt-5-6-ga.detail: Opens to all users after a two-week federal review, alongside the launch of ChatGPT Work.

kimi-k3.title: Kimi K3
kimi-k3.detail: Moonshot AI releases a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model with a 1-million-token context window.

gemini-3-6-flash.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash
gemini-3-6-flash.detail: Google releases three Flash models and says pretraining of Gemini 4 has begun.

openai-astra-math.title: Astra solves ten hard problems
openai-astra-math.detail: A new OpenAI model solves ten problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science that had stood open for more than a decade.

qwen-3-8-max.title: Qwen3.8-Max
qwen-3-8-max.detail: Alibaba releases a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 95 billion active parameters and pledges to open its weights.

gpt-5-6-cyber.title: GPT-5.6 Cyber
gpt-5-6-cyber.detail: A cybersecurity-specific model offered only to vetted partners.

grok-4-6.title: Grok 4.6
grok-4-6.detail: Ties GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

nvidia-openai-ohio.title: Nvidia backs OpenAI financing
nvidia-openai-ohio.detail: Up to $105 billion supports the first 4.25 gigawatts of compute at the Ohio campus, coming online from 2028.

claude-fable-5-1.title: Claude Fable 5.1
claude-fable-5-1.detail: Base pricing is unchanged; cache-read prices drop by 75%.

gpt-6-astra.title: GPT-6 Astra
gpt-6-astra.detail: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 Astra in stages, with cybersecurity program participants first.

claude-opus-5-5.title: Claude Opus 5.5
claude-opus-5-5.detail: Approaches Fable 5.1 on most tasks at 40% lower running cost than Opus 5.

gpt-6-sol-luna.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna
gpt-6-sol-luna.detail: OpenAI launches GPT-6's flagship and lightweight models at half the API price of the 5.6 series.

gemini-4-argon.title: Gemini 4 Argon
gemini-4-argon.detail: Google unveils a new frontier model with the per-response output limit raised to 1 million tokens.

forecast-agent-teams-speculative.title: Agent teams on long tasks (speculative)
forecast-agent-teams-speculative.detail: Scenario forecast (2027–2029): teams of AI agents may divide work, check each other and deliver continuously in software development and research. This assumes mature permissions, verification and failure recovery; humans remain accountable for complex tasks. Confidence in direction: medium. Year is a browsing anchor.

forecast-personal-ai-speculative.title: Personal AI and on-device coordination (speculative)
forecast-personal-ai-speculative.detail: Scenario forecast (2027–2030): personal assistants may work across phones and computers, with more everyday tasks handled on-device. Adoption depends on power use, privacy permissions and reliable memory; complex tasks may still rely on the cloud. Confidence in direction: medium. Year is a browsing anchor.

forecast-controlled-robotics-speculative.title: Robots enter controlled settings (speculative)
forecast-controlled-robotics-speculative.detail: Scenario forecast (2028–2031): robots in warehouses, factories and labs may take on more multi-step operations, expanding first in jobs with controlled environments. Cost, safety and fault handling still limit adoption; a robot in every home is not the baseline scenario. Confidence in direction: medium to low. Year is a browsing anchor.

forecast-kurzweil-2029.title: Forecast: AI reaches human-level intelligence
forecast-kurzweil-2029.detail: In The Singularity Is Nearer, Kurzweil reaffirms that AI will reach human-level intelligence by 2029.

forecast-science-loop-speculative.title: Closed-loop AI science (speculative)
forecast-science-loop-speculative.detail: Scenario forecast (2029–2031): in some materials and life-science problems, AI may link hypotheses, experimental design and analysis, with automated equipment shortening iterations. Only reproducible experimental validation counts as a breakthrough, and it does not mean drugs will be approved right away. Confidence in direction: medium to low. Year is a browsing anchor.

forecast-epoch-2e29.title: Forecast: 2e29 FLOP training runs
forecast-epoch-2e29.detail: Epoch AI estimates that training runs of about 2×10²⁹ floating-point operations will likely be feasible by 2030.

forecast-iea-datacentre.title: Forecast: data center electricity doubles
forecast-iea-datacentre.detail: The International Energy Agency projects global data center electricity use of about 945 TWh in 2030, more than double the 2024 level.

forecast-grid-compute-speculative.title: Compute and grid build out together (speculative)
forecast-grid-compute-speculative.detail: Scenario forecast (2028–2031): AI demand may drive coordinated expansion of data centers, power grids, energy storage and cooling. The IEA's 2030 electricity projection grounds the demand; the build-out pace in this scenario remains constrained by grid connection, financing and supply chains, and does not imply energy has become limitlessly cheap. Confidence in direction: fairly high on demand, medium on build-out pace. Year is a browsing anchor.

forecast-interactive-worlds-speculative.title: Interactive worlds and simulation training (speculative)
forecast-interactive-worlds-speculative.detail: Scenario forecast (2029–2031): interactive generated worlds may be used for creative work, training and robot simulation. Long-run consistency, physical accuracy and cost will determine where they are usable; a playable scene is not a trustworthy simulation of reality. Confidence in direction: medium to low. Year is a browsing anchor.

forecast-metaculus-agi.title: Forecast: artificial general intelligence arrives
forecast-metaculus-agi.detail: The Metaculus community's median forecast for the public announcement of the first general AI system is around 2032 (subject to change).

forecast-iter-dt.title: Forecast: ITER deuterium-tritium operation
forecast-iter-dt.detail: Under its 2024 baseline, ITER plans to begin research operation in 2034 and deuterium-tritium operation in 2039.

forecast-kurzweil-2045.title: Forecast: the Singularity
forecast-kurzweil-2045.detail: Kurzweil predicts humans will merge with machines by 2045, an event he calls "the Singularity."

forecast-population-2050.title: Forecast: world population about 9.7 billion
forecast-population-2050.detail: The medium scenario of the UN's World Population Prospects 2024 projects a world population of about 9.7 billion in 2050.

forecast-population-peak.title: Forecast: world population peaks
forecast-population-peak.detail: The UN projects world population will peak at about 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s and then decline.

rea-software-reconstruction.title: Dawn of a Software Openness Era
rea-software-reconstruction.detail: REA connects reverse-engineering tools to coding agents. An October hands-on test used Opus 5.5 with REA to rebuild an app’s keep-awake feature. We see falling barriers to understanding and reconstruction as the dawn of a software openness era; the original software has not thereby become open source or openly licensed.

population.label: World population
population.note: Before 1950, figures are historical reconstructions such as HYDE, with errors of up to several tens of percent; from 2025 on, they are UN medium-variant projections.
population.sourceName: Our World in Data (HYDE 3.3, Gapminder, UN World Population Prospects 2024 medium variant)

energy.label: Total human primary energy power
energy.note: Average power = annual energy use (joules) ÷ seconds in a year. Before 1800, per-capita estimates are multiplied by population, with large errors; the substitution method inflates the share of renewables.
energy.sourceName: Our World in Data global primary energy (Smil 2017 + Energy Institute, substitution method); before 1800: Syvitski et al. 2020 per-capita energy use × HYDE population

compute.label: Compute per dollar
compute.unit: floating-point operations per second per dollar (FLOP/s per $, nominal dollars)
compute.note: Calculated as 1e9 ÷ cost in dollars per GFLOPS. Precision varies across points (mostly double precision for 1945–2000, mostly GPU single precision afterwards); shows orders of magnitude only.
compute.sourceName: Wikipedia: Floating point operations per second — Cost of computing (hardware cost per GFLOPS, not adjusted for inflation)

messaging.label: Fastest delivery time for a message from London to New York
messaging.note: Sailing ships and steamships use typical England–North America voyages; the 1927 radiotelephone figure is estimated from a 5,570 km light path, and the 2015 figure is half of a 59 ms fiber round trip.
messaging.sourceName: Wikipedia: Mayflower, Black Ball Line (transatlantic packet), SS Great Western, Transatlantic telegraph cable, Transatlantic communications cable, Hibernia Networks

travel.label: Fastest speed reached by humans
travel.note: The highest speed humans could reach at the time: walking, galloping on horseback, rail, aircraft, rockets and human spaceflight. The start date for horseback riding (domestication) is disputed.
travel.sourceName: Wikipedia: Preferred walking speed, Horse gait, Land speed record for rail vehicles, Flight airspeed record, Apollo 10; NASA (Vostok 1)
